rows.what the ink shows: An initial rising hook, a separate high apostrophe-like stroke and a terminal upright survive, but the broad double cancellation fills the intervening baseline bodies; e and s cannot be distinguished.

The left end has a tall looped f-like stem with a deep lower return and one short right shoulder. The remaining low strokes run into the cancellation and the adjoining blackened body, so acile and the boundary before M1199 are not separately recoverable.

Between the left f-like beginning and the visible following que is a dense blackened group with two small surviving white counters, an upright and a low diagonal spur. Those remnants do not establish a word or its boundary with M1198, even in the 6x contrast view.

The first word retains a c-shaped lower hook, raised apostrophe and t upright, while its middle is blackened. After a clear gap, un retains a low u trough and adjoining n shoulder; the next word has a long p stem and final looped j descent, but its intervening ro bodies lie under the deletion stroke. The inserted on sait que is a separate upper layer.

A tall initial L-shaped upright and foot remain, followed by a dark flattened body; the second group retains a descending p-like return, a late t upright and a separate high point. The deletion covers the a and the central/final letter bodies, so the whole proposed phrase is not secure.

There is one looped initial body followed by crossed x arms and a tall t in the heavy group near x783-856; the next high point stands above a low continuation resembling erieure, rather than a clear baseline stop. No distinct second ext onset is visible for the source's deleted ext. plus extérieure allocation, so the marked reading and allocation remain uncertain.

A tall oval loop survives above the deletion and a small pale counter remains at its lower right, but the lower junction and terminal body are crossed repeatedly. The surviving lower counter does not securely distinguish a from another short looped ending.

At the right of the line, a narrow upright loop and one small following rise project above a thick horizontal cancellation. That stroke conceals the lower joins and any remaining n shoulder, so the two-letter reading cannot be established from the exposed bodies.

The deleted word has a clear central descender and a separate short curved accent above its right half. The thick cancellation merges the initial bowl and the remaining baseline letters, preventing recovery of the complete apres sequence despite the surviving accent and descender.

Two small rises at the left and two short uprights near the right remain above the crossing-out, with isolated dark marks below and to the right. The long middle stroke obscures the intervening letter bodies and prevents a secure count of the proposed m-u-l-t sequence or its terminal punctuation.

The right-hand a has its own closed bowl, right downstroke and separate lower-right 1. After the preceding visible epsilon with sigma index, the marked residue shows a short upper dash and an open bent lower body; cancellation crosses the baseline, so neither a second epsilon with tau index nor the extra baseline sigma of the other candidate can be counted securely.

All current-page mark boundaries were read. An initial broad TSV grep also printed adjacent-page metadata rows; no later-page image or page text was opened or inspected.
The actual primary interval includes document reading and report preparation; it is not claimed as uninterrupted active visual inspection.
